title: The Arrival

beats.what: Boyd counts every bullet in the settlement, frames it as last-resort planning; Kenny pushes back
Elgin is stitched up by Kristi after Sara took his eye; Donna enforces silence about the act
Donna coerces Elgin into a cover story under threat of the box
New arrivals: a father and daughter crash near town during a seizure; community scrambles to extract them
Marielle identifies the father's seizure as similar to Elgin's and Ethan's arrival episodes
Tabitha confronts Jade about whether to tell people what they remembered; Jade pushes disclosure, Tabitha hesitates

character_beats.beat: Wants to protect the community but is already planning for mass death; counts bullets for a mass killing as a mercy option rather than fighting for a way out
Wants order and community cohesion but uses blackmail to suppress truth, compromising the integrity she claims to protect
Wants to share what she and Jade remembered but fears it will be weaponized the way Sara's visions were

key_lines.line: The day may come when the only thing we get to decide is how we choose to leave.
key_lines.why: Boyd articulates suicidal community-exit as legitimate planning, not defeat

key_lines.line: I just need to make sure there's enough, just in case.
key_lines.why: Euphemism that names the plan without naming it

key_lines.line: Now I think this place does bad things to good people.
key_lines.why: Kristi reframes Sara's violence as environmental rather than moral

key_lines.line: What's easier to believe, that whatever is keeping us here put those thoughts in our heads to torture us...
key_lines.why: Tabitha names the epistemological trap at the heart of the season

open_loops: Who is the new father (Sophia's father) and why did he seize on approach to town, like other arrivals?
Donna has secured Elgin's silence with a threat, but the truth about Sara and Tillie remains unburied
Boyd's bullet stockpile implies a plan he has not stated aloud to the community

contradiction.wants: To be the protector who gives the community hope and fights for survival
contradiction.does: Counts bullets for a potential mass mercy-killing, treating defeat as inevitable

tone_notes: Densest dialogue in the episode clusters in minutes 22-25 (density 226-244 words/min) during the car-crash rescue, producing a chaotic urgency that contrasts with the eerie low-density stretches in minutes 5-8 (34-43) during the night aftermath. Two major silences: 48:47-49:38 (50 sec) and 31:52-32:39 (47 sec) both fall in sequences where characters are moving through the dark or sitting with unspoken decisions.
